scope: Current connecta behavior, not SDK capability alone. Supported means the described scope has tests; partial names its gaps. Planned includes work deferred outside the rework's scope and unimplemented optional core features. #703 decisions may be superseded by a later record.

features.notes: SDK serves both eras. Connecta-owned admission, origin/access, pool, and deadline refusals use JSON-RPC error bodies with application codes outside reserved ranges and omitted unknown request IDs validated against the modern SDK schema; auth-adapter-owned refusal bodies remain adapter-defined pending Phase 3 inbound auth.
SDK auto negotiation upward and downstream, with explicit known-legacy opt-out.

SDK envelope clientCapabilities and clientInfo are bound to request-local meta-tool context. Direct and program activity retain only allowlisted ASCII client name/version facts, bounded to 64/32 characters. Invalid facts are absent at the record, SQL write/read, and operator UI boundaries; capabilities and other metadata never enter activity.

Fresh upward server and request-local downstream clients; legacy session cleanup stays request-scoped. Concurrent stateless requests share only isolate-level admission queues, which wake each queued request, call, and execute_code program in its own request and async context, whichever request released the slot.
Legacy initialize and modern server/discover preserve configured title, websiteUrl, and icons.

server/discover advertises supported modern revisions, tools and skill resources capabilities, the served Skills extension map, the caller-scoped dev.connecta/endpoint vendor extension on discovery and legacy initialize, configured server identity, and private one-hour cache hints.

Fetch-native HTTP supports both eras, private cache hints, address x-mcp-header declarations, and JSON-RPC route refusals. Auth-adapter-owned refusal bodies remain adapter-defined pending Phase 3 inbound auth. A remoteMcp connector may send its downstream transport through a deployment fetch, such as a Workers service binding, confined to its configured origin and redirect policy.
The prescribed deployments expose fetch/HTTP; no connecta stdio entrypoint.

Clerk binds JWT and opaque OAuth tokens to the canonical MCP resource and owns its protected-resource challenge with scopes. Cloudflare Access is supported for humans on direct Worker invocations through edge-validated application AUD and ctx.access; Node uses Clerk. Machines are agents declared in code, each with one stored cta_ token that rotates with immediate cutover; static bearer is removed. Downstream auth and auth elicitation follow-ups remain in #707. Pre-layout-3 OAuth grants are refused as absent with a credential-free operator warning; migrate on 0.37.1 or reauthorize. Maintainers listed in code receive the whole catalog at plain /mcp and alone reach the maintainer operator routes after auth; maintainers belong to no pool, and every other person is listed in at most one pool, which plain /mcp serves them; each named pool admits only its static members and serves exactly its tools, agents at /agent/<pool>, and every /mcp/<anything> path is the MCP 404 before auth. Agent endpoints accept only cta_ tokens, ignore Access context, answer a machine-only Bearer challenge, and publish no protected-resource metadata; every other spelling of the agent namespace is refused before auth, and human endpoints refuse cta_. Protected-resource metadata stays public for credential-free OAuth discovery.
Downstream discovery persists across callbacks and binds grants to the validated issuer.

Self-hosted CIMD defaults on configured public HTTPS deployments, with DCR fallback and issuer-bound pre-registered remoteMcp clients. Status reports the selected path. The draft revision's changelog moves the Client ID Metadata Document reference from draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00 to -03 and requires implementations that support CIMD to follow -03. No regression yet checks the self-hosted document against -03.

PKCE, state, issuer, origin, and Clerk resource-audience binding have regressions. Callback errors require validated state and issuer, then atomically consume the consent and discard its verifier. Disconnect attempts advertised RFC 7009 revocation after local removal; failures are typed and payload-free. Downstream request auth never passes an inbound token through: opt-in principal forwarding gives the deployment's resolver only the admitted person's reference (agents only when accepted), refuses other callers before resolving, and never reuses a client across principals. Challenged downstream resource_metadata must share the configured remoteMcp resource origin (parsed scheme, host, and port); status, starts, and live calls refuse foreign challenges before SDK discovery without exposing challenged hosts. All SDK discovery reads, including callbacks and unchallenged flows, discard foreign cached resource metadata and rediscover same-origin, retaining issuer binding. Same-origin paths and Google per-tool metadata remain accepted. Passive OAuth MCP requests require a credential after the SDK token read regardless of provider replacement; missing tokens return typed recovery before fetch. Verified unsent writes count as failed through private request provenance, while dispatched writes retain ambiguous outcomes. Explicit authorization challenges, setup and refresh flows remain supported.

The current meta-tools are listed, with execute_read_code on writable meta endpoints; downstream pages assemble complete catalogs. Host-specific tool _meta hints (anthropic/alwaysLoad on one meta entry tool, anthropic/maxResultSizeChars derived from configured result caps) are config-derived and non-normative.

Direct and program calls work; both direct-call tools declare the address parameter header. The three structured-only meta-tools declare an open outputSchema; native-content direct-call tools omit it. A native pool binds each wire name to the tool's classification and takes the route the name selects, so a client's resent read name is refused before dispatch once the tool is a write. Maintained-provider hostile HTTP acknowledgements remain failures even after a vendor commits; a subsequent read reconciles state without replaying the physical write.

Read/write routing fails closed. A readOnly endpoint or connector lists write tools in search_tools results and describe with callable: false, omits them from a native pool's tools/list, and refuses every write call with read_only_endpoint. execute_code's annotations follow the endpoint, and the client owns approval.

Validate tool arguments locally before dispatch. Recovery echoes omit writeOnly values at nested properties, array items and prefixes, local references, and allOf. Ambiguous alternatives, unresolved references, unsupported sensitivity rules, and traversal limits withhold args with argsRedacted; explicit retries require original arguments.

Downstream structured output is SDK-validated across every catalog page. The three structured-only meta-tools advertise open output schemas (required keys and top-level types) that successful structured content satisfies, and the server validates each successful result against the full contract before sending it; both SDK edges exempt isError responses, but some hosts validate them too, so an error result either satisfies the advertised schema or carries its JSON in content alone. Direct-call tools omit outputSchema because default-mode successes return native content; value-mode and error envelopes still mirror complete JSON. A downstream outputSchema is compiled by the SDK's runtime validator: Ajv with fast-uri 3.1.8 on Node, @cfworker/json-schema on Workers. Node refuses to compile a $id or $ref with an invalid URI scheme, which Workers compiles and validates, and a $ref that resolves only through a percent-encoded slash, which Workers compiles but fails when validation reaches the reference. On Node such a call is refused before dispatch as a non-retryable connector_call_failed that names the operator as the one to fix the downstream schema.

Default-mode direct-call successes preserve downstream content and bounded notice-first previews, omit structuredContent, and carry format in _meta["dev.connecta/format"]. Value-mode and error results carry complete data in structuredContent and serialized JSON in content. Guest emission permits text, image and audio only; internal result pages retain their text and paging fields. Program calls transparently reconstruct bounded oversized values through the same stash and return larger values as format:paged handles for connecta.result(handle, { page?, offset?, maxBytes? }); completed writes remain successful and are never repeated for output.

Programs read downstream resources with connector-qualified connecta.read URIs, whole-connector grants, request-scoped auth, admission, deadlines and credential redaction. Remote reads require exact advertised resources or bounded, traversal-safe RFC 6570 template matches from complete paginated, host-auth-partitioned inventories. Skill-only upward resources/list and resources/read use the caller-view skills registry, including deployment skill source files, with private five-minute hints for local-only views and zero TTL when downstream skills are enabled. Program-facing listing/template discovery and subscriptions remain unimplemented; no general upward resource proxy is claimed.
Deferred by #703's Deferred row; no prompts advertised today.

Auth URL elicitation on capable 2026-07-28 hosts with short identity-checked connect links that name a stored sealed handoff (falling back to the sealed link when storage refuses it), ordinary recovery fallback, and a handoff on decline or cancel. Deployments and pools can turn the auth prompt off with authElicitation: false, and a host marked x-anthropic-client: Cowork, which declares URL elicitation but never shows it, gets the ordinary handoff instead of a prompt. Incapable hosts receive the same signed OAuth or operator credential handoff as explicit authorization in direct, program, and catalog auth errors, reused once per connector per request without forcing reauthorization. Direct calls relay downstream form and URL elicitation only when the client declares that mode, with namespaced keys, validated bare responses, HTTPS URLs without known credentials, and agent-output redaction. Programs keep downstream elicitation unsupported; sampling and roots remain declined under #703. Auth writes still elicit only before invocation, independently of downstream continuations.

Auth recovery uses createRequestStateCodec and host-owned invocation facts; writes elicit auth only before invocation and entered reads require unchanged fresh classifications. Direct calls now relay downstream state inside vault encryption and the signed codec envelope, bound to principal, endpoint/pool, connector, original and resolved addresses, arguments digest, round, expiry, and a one-use storage CAS nonce. Original downstream keys stay encrypted behind numbered namespaced keys. Three prompts and a ten-minute window span auth-to-downstream composition; payload and response limits apply. Programs refuse downstream input with a direct-call nextAction. Sampling, roots, prompts, and other deferred request kinds are not relayed. Continuation failures reuse the invocation's schema-filtered snapshot and direct-call guidance requires original arguments for partial or absent echoes.

subscriptions/listen is deferred by #703's Deferred row. The Events extension carries its optional event-type list-change notifications on this stream through an added filter field; events/poll works without it.
Request abort/deadline cancellation closes calls and scopes; protocol-level cancel notification behavior has no connecta-specific regression.
No connecta-specific progress forwarding or notification contract; adopt when a request requires it.

Private upward tools/list and server/discover hints and SQL-backed SDK tool/resource/template listing ResponseCacheStore honor bounded downstream TTL and intake redaction. Host auth mode constrains sharing; public hints never remove private credential, principal, pool or endpoint partitions. OAuth credential changes fence reuse within one epoch. Connection-owned notifications fence late listings, and serialized listings preserve cancellation through cleanup. Resource read payloads are never cached. Completed wire tool refreshes expose previous/new digest observations for the planned Phase 4 drift-event integration.

SDK Client.listTools aggregates downstream pages complete-or-failure. Intake refuses loops, nonprogress, invalid header declarations, and partial failures before SDK caching. Upward pagination of meta-tools remains planned.
No completion/complete handler today; resources/prompts adoption determines its useful scope.
Bounded 2020-12 validation exists, including dependentSchemas/unevaluatedProperties; arbitrary dialect conformance is not claimed.
No connecta traceparent/tracestate/baggage propagation contract; per-request envelope threading comes first.
Deprecated upstream and not adopted under the plan.
Deprecated upstream and not adopted under the plan.
MCP logging is deprecated upstream and not adopted. Local operator logs are a separate concern.
SDK initialize and legacy sessions remain for older hosts; connecta closes downstream sessions with their request.
MCP Apps is Stable upstream and deferred here by #703's Deferred row.

Beta under SEP-3392 (SEP-2640); breaking revisions may reuse the extension ID. modelcontextprotocol/ext-skills tagged its first schema, v0.1.0, on 2026-11-20, with the specification under specification/beta/. The released settings define no revision; explicit downstream revisions are refused. Native skills/list and skills/get share one registry with skill-only resources and both text readers. Local manifests, five-entry pages, opt-in downstream proxying, whole-connector grants, byte preservation and the credential-redaction exception are enforced. Deployment skill sources (inlineSkills) serve complete multi-file manifests with SHA-256 digests, byte-exact text and blob reads, frontmatter equal to the served SKILL.md, pool-scoped visibility indistinguishable from absence, and supporting-file reads on both text readers; a source with nothing to serve fails the listing while built-in skills and connector guides stay readable. githubSkills serves a directory of a GitHub repository from storage-published snapshots keyed by the directory's Git tree, revalidated after freshFor under a storage lease, resumable after an interrupted sync, kept in service with one typed warning on every failed check, rate limit, truncated tree or invalid skill, with its token sent only to api.github.com and absent from every output, log and stored value, and its frontmatter read as full YAML 1.2 equal to the served SKILL.md (fixture GitHub API). Directory reading (resources/directory/read) remains undeclared.

Tasks, including downstream task polling, are deferred by #703's Deferred row. Tasks is Beta with Core as its stated destination; draft SEP-3570 targets the September 2027 revision. The extension client matrix now lists host support.

Machine clients are code-declared agents using cta_ access tokens or explicitly bound Vercel OIDC workloads. The OAuth client credentials extension is not implemented or negotiated. The extension is Stable.
Inbound human auth is Clerk or Worker Access. Edge-managed Access is not negotiation of this extension. The extension is Stable.

Beta under SEP-3415. Not implemented or negotiated, and no implementation is scheduled; #1483 tracks the evaluation. If adopted, poll delivery (events/poll) is the candidate: it holds no protocol-required server state and fits cursor-backed api() connectors. Push (events/stream) and webhook (events/subscribe) delivery are not planned.

Beta under SEP-2127. Not implemented and not scheduled: no card or ai-catalog document is published. A card would carry deployment-level identity and connection metadata; server/discover and legacy initialize already serve the configured identity, and SEP-2127 keeps caller-scoped tools and capabilities out of cards. Revisit when a supported host reads cards.
